claim: Drosophila orco mutant (orco1/orco1) larvae show reduction in lamellocyte formation in the lymph gland at 24 hours post-infection compared to control (w1118).
source: Compared to (A–A') control (w1118), orco1/orco1 mutant larvae show reduction in lamellocyte in (B, C) lymph gland (n = 20, ***p<0.0001 compared to w1118, n = 18)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B-C with statistical analysis (p<0.0001) and quantification of lamellocyte counts in the lymph gland.

claim: Specifically ablating Or42a (Or42a-Gal4; UAS-Hid) causes reduction in lamellocytes in the lymph gland at 24 hours post-infection.
source: Specifically ablating Or42a (Or42a-Gal4; UAS-Hid) causes reduction in lamellocytes in (E, F) lymph gland (n = 24, ***p<0.0001 compared to Or42a-Gal4/+, n = 24)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E-F with statistical analysis (p<0.0001) and quantification of lamellocyte counts.

claim: Blocking neuronal GABA bio-synthesis in Kurs6+ neurons (Kurs6-Gal4; UAS-Gad1RNAi) causes reduction in lamellocytes in the lymph gland at 24 hours post-infection.
source: Blocking neuronal GABA bio-synthesis in Kurs6+ neurons (Kurs6-Gal4; UAS-Gad1RNAi) recapitulates lamellocyte reduction in (H, I) lymph gland (n = 22, ***p<0.0001 compared to Kurs6-Gal4/+, n = 18)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H-I with statistical analysis (p<0.0001) and quantification of lamellocyte counts.

claim: Olfactory neuron ablation (Orco-Gal4, UAS-Hid, rpr) inhibits lamellocyte differentiation in the lymph gland at 24 hours post-infection.
source: Olfactory neuron ablation inhibits lamellocyte differentiation both in the (A) lymph gland Orco-Gal4/+ (n = 14, control) and Orco-Gal4, UAS-Hid, rpr (n = 16, ***p=0.0001)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A with statistical analysis (p=0.0001) and quantification of lamellocyte counts.

claim: Larvae reared on minimal odor food (MOF) show lamellocyte defect in the lymph gland at 24 hours post-infection compared to regular food (RF).
source: Quantification of (C) lymph gland lamellocyte counts in RF (n = 11), MOF (n = 12, ***p=0.0002), and MOF rescue with food odors (n = 14, *p=0.0113)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C with statistical analysis (p=0.0002) and quantification of lamellocyte counts.

claim: Supplementing minimal odor food with food odors restores lamellocyte formation in the lymph gland.
source: Quantification of (C) lymph gland lamellocyte counts in RF (n = 11), MOF (n = 12, ***p=0.0002), and MOF rescue with food odors (n = 14, *p=0.0113)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing that food odor supplementation partially restores lamellocyte counts (p=0.0113) compared to MOF condition.

claim: Blocking projection neuron signaling (GH146-Gal4; UAS-ChATRNAi) leads to reduction in lamellocyte numbers in circulation at 48 hours post-infection.
source: Blocking projection neuron signaling (GH146-Gal4; UAS-ChATRNAi) leads to reduction in lamellocyte numbers. Quantifications of total circulating lamellocytes in GH146>/+ (control, n = 43) and GH146>ChATRNAi (n = 36, ***p<0.0001).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1G with statistical analysis (p<0.0001) and quantification of circulating lamellocyte counts.

claim: Orco-Gal4 expression in uninfected and infected (6HPI) conditions remains unchanged in the dorsal organ ganglion.
source: Expression of Orco-Gal4 (green, Orco-Gal4; UAS-2xEGFP) in (A) uninfected and (B) infected (6HPI) conditions remains unchanged. Arrows indicate Dorsal organ ganglion.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A-B showing consistent Orco-Gal4 expression patterns.

claim: No expression of Orco-Gal4 is detected in cells of the lymph gland or in the posterior signaling center (PSC) in uninfected and infected (6HPI) conditions.
source: No expression of Orco-Gal4 (green, Orco-Gal4; UAS-2xEGFP) is detected in cells of the lymph gland or in the posterior signaling center PSC (Antp, red) in (C) uninfected and (D) infected (6HPI) condition.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C-D showing absence of Orco-Gal4 expression in lymph gland and PSC.

claim: Antp+ cell numbers per lymph gland remain unchanged in Orco-Gal4; UAS-2xEGFP and Orco-Gal4; UAS-Hid conditions in both uninfected and infected (6HPI) states.
source: Quantification of Antp + cells per lymph gland in Orco-Gal4; UAS-2xEGFP, uninfected (n = 11), Orco-Gal4; UAS-2xEGFP, 6HPI (n = 12, ns compared to Orco-Gal4; UAS-2xEGFP, uninfected), Orco-Gal4; UAS-Hid, uninfected (n = 12, ns compared Orco-Gal4; UAS-2xEGFP, uninfected), and Orco-Gal4; UAS-Hid, 6HPI (n = 12, ns compared to Orco-Gal4; UAS-2xEGFP, 6HPI) showed no change in their numbers.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2E with statistical analysis showing no significant changes (ns).

claim: Or42a-Gal4 expression in uninfected and infected (6HPI) conditions remains unchanged in the dorsal organ ganglion.
source: Expression of Or42a-Gal4 (green, Or42a-Gal4; UAS-2xEGFP) in (F) uninfected and (G) infected condition (6HPI) remains unchanged. Arrows indicate Dorsal organ ganglion.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2F-G showing consistent Or42a-Gal4 expression patterns.

claim: No expression of Or42a-Gal4 is detected in cells of the lymph gland or in the PSC in uninfected and infected (6HPI) conditions.
source: No expression of Or42a-Gal4 (green, Or42a-Gal4; UAS-2xEGFP) is detected in cells of the lymph gland or in the PSC (Antp, red) in (H) uninfected and (I) infected (6HPI) conditions.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2H-I showing absence of Or42a-Gal4 expression in lymph gland and PSC.

claim: Antp+ cell numbers per lymph gland remain unchanged in Or42a-Gal4; UAS-2xEGFP and Or42a-Gal4; UAS-Hid conditions in both uninfected and infected (6HPI) states.
source: Quantification of Antp + cells per lymph gland in Or42a-Gal4; UAS-2xEGFP, uninfected (n = 16), and Or42a-Gal4; UAS-2xEGFP, 6HPI (n = 12, ns compared to Or42a-Gal4; UAS-2xEGFP, uninfected), Or42a-Gal4; UAS-Hid, uninfected (n = 10, ns compared to Or42a-Gal4; UAS-2xEGFP, uninfected), and Or42a-Gal4; UAS-Hid, 6HPI (n = 8, ns, compared to Or42a-Gal4; UAS-2xEGFP, 6HPI) showed no change in their numbers.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2J with statistical analysis showing no significant changes (ns).

claim: Kurs6-Gal4 expression in the larval brain shows no change in uninfected and infected (6HPI) conditions.
source: Expression of Kurs6-Gal4 (green, Kurs6-Gal4; UAS-mCD8GFP) in the larval brain (indicated by while dotted lines, and zoomed in image in the white box for better clarity) shows no change in (K) uninfected and (L) infected conditions (6HPI).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2K-L showing consistent Kurs6-Gal4 expression patterns in the brain.

claim: No expression of Kurs6-Gal4 is seen in the lymph gland blood cells and the PSC in uninfected and infected (6HPI) conditions.
source: No expression of Kurs6-Gal4 (green, Kurs6-Gal4; UAS-mCD8GFP) is seen in the lymph gland blood cells and the PSC (Antp, red), in (M) uninfected and (N) infected (6HPI) condition.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2M-N showing absence of Kurs6-Gal4 expression in lymph gland and PSC.

claim: Antp+ cell numbers per lymph gland remain unchanged in Kurs6-Gal4; UAS-mCD8GFP and Kurs6-Gal4; UAS-mCD8GFP; UAS-Gad1RNAi conditions in both uninfected and infected (6HPI) states.
source: Quantification of Antp + cells per lymph gland in Kurs6-Gal4; UAS-mCD8GFP, uninfected, (n = 18), Kurs6-Gal4; UAS-mCD8GFP, 6HPI (n = 10, ns compared to Kurs6-Gal4; UAS-mCD8GFP, uninfected), Kurs6-Gal4; UAS-mCD8GFP; UAS-Gad1RNAi, uninfected (n = 18, ns compared to Kurs6-Gal4; UAS-mCD8GFP, uninfected) and Kurs6-Gal4; UAS-mCD8GFP; UAS-Gad1RNAi, 6HPI (n = 23, ns, compared to Kurs6-Gal4; UAS-mCD8GFP, 6HPI) showed no change in their numbers.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2O with statistical analysis showing no significant changes (ns).

claim: Or49a-Gal4 expression in uninfected and infected (6HPI) conditions remains unchanged in the dorsal organ ganglion.
source: Expression of Or49a-Gal4 (green, Or49a-Gal4; UAS-2xEGFP) in (P) uninfected and (Q) infected condition (6HPI) remains unchanged. Arrows indicate Dorsal organ ganglion.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2P-Q showing consistent Or49a-Gal4 expression patterns.

claim: No expression of Or49a-Gal4 is seen in the lymph gland blood cells and the PSC in uninfected and infected (6HPI) conditions.
source: No expression of Or49a-Gal4 (green, Or49a-Gal4; UAS-2xEGFP) is seen in the lymph gland blood cells and the PSC (Antp, red), in (r) uninfected and (s) infected (6HPI) conditions.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2R-S showing absence of Or49a-Gal4 expression in lymph gland and PSC.

claim: Antp+ cell numbers per lymph gland remain unchanged in Or49a-Gal4; UAS-2xEGFP and Or49a-Gal4; UAS-Hid conditions in both uninfected and infected (6HPI) states.
source: Quantification of Antp + cells per lymph gland in Or49a-Gal4; UAS-2xEGFP, uninfected, (n = 10), and Or49a-Gal4; UAS-2xEGFP, 6HPI (n = 8, ns compared to Or49a-Gal4; UAS-2xEGFP, uninfected), Or49a-Gal4; UAS-Hid, uninfected (n = 11, ns compared to Or49a-Gal4; UAS-2xEGFP, uninfected) and 6HPI (n = 9, ns, compared to Or49a-Gal4; UAS-2xEGFP, 6HPI) showed no change in their numbers.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2T with statistical analysis showing no significant changes (ns).

claim: GABA transporter (Gat) expression is elevated in control lymph gland at 6HPI compared to uninfected state.
source: Uniform GABA transporter (Gat) expression is detected in control (Hml△-Gal4, UAS-GFP) lymph gland from (B) Uninfected Drosophila larvae. In comparison to uninfected lymph gland, (C) Gat expression is elevated in lymph gland at 6HPI.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2B-C and quantification in Figure 2D showing approximately twofold increase in Gat expression at 6HPI.

claim: Compared to uninfected control lymph gland, almost twofold increase in Gat expression is observed at 6HPI.
source: Relative fold change in Gat expression in control lymph gland from uninfected and infected states at 6HPI. Compared to uninfected control lymph gland (Hml△-Gal4, UAS-GFP/+, n = 15), almost twofold increase in Gat expression is observed at 6HPI (Hml△-Gal4, UAS-GFP/+, n = 16, ***p<0.0001).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 2D with statistical analysis (p<0.0001) showing twofold increase in Gat expression.

claim: Intracellular GABA (iGABA) levels are elevated in control lymph gland at 6HPI compared to uninfected state.
source: Control (dome-MESO>GFP/+) lymph glands from (E) Uninfected Drosophila larvae show punctated iGABA staining in all blood cells (anti-GABA antibody staining in 1X PBS + 0.3%Triton X-100). In comparison to (E), iGABA levels detected in (F) lymph gland at 6HPI is elevated.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2E-F and quantification in Figure 2G showing twofold increase in iGABA levels at 6HPI.

claim: Compared to uninfected control lymph gland, a twofold increase in iGABA expression is observed at 6HPI.
source: Relative fold change in iGABA levels in uninfected and infected control lymph glands at 6HPI. Compared to uninfected control lymph gland (dome-MESO-Gal4, UAS-GFP/+, n = 9), a twofold increase in iGABA expression is observed at 6HPI (dome-MESO-Gal4, UAS-GFP/+, n = 11, ***p<0.0001).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 2G with statistical analysis (p<0.0001) showing twofold increase in iGABA levels.

claim: Loss of progenitor Gat function (dome-MESO-Gal4, UAS-GFP; UAS-GatRNAi) leads to reduced iGABA levels in uninfected state.
source: Loss of progenitor Gat function (dome-MESO-Gal4, UAS-GFP; UAS-GatRNAi) leads to reduced iGABA levels both in (H) uninfected and (I) infected states as compared to control (dome-MESO-Gal4, UAS-GFP/+) in (E) uninfected and (F) infected states, respectively.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2H and quantification in Figure 2J showing reduced iGABA levels in GatRNAi condition.

claim: Loss of progenitor Gat function (dome-MESO-Gal4, UAS-GFP; UAS-GatRNAi) leads to reduced iGABA levels at 6HPI.
source: Loss of progenitor Gat function (dome-MESO-Gal4, UAS-GFP; UAS-GatRNAi) leads to reduced iGABA levels both in (H) uninfected and (I) infected states as compared to control (dome-MESO-Gal4, UAS-GFP/+) in (E) uninfected and (F) infected states, respectively.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2I and quantification in Figure 2K showing reduced iGABA levels in GatRNAi condition at 6HPI.

claim: Larvae over-expressing Gat in progenitor cells (dome-MESO-Gal4, UAS-GFP; UAS-Gat) show an increase in iGABA levels in blood cells compared to control.
source: Lymph glands from (C) control (dome-MESO>GFP/+) uninfected larvae show punctated iGABA (green) staining in all blood cells of lymph gland while (D) larvae over-expressing Gat in progenitor cells (dome-MESO-Gal4, UAS-GFP; UAS-Gat) showed an increase in iGABA levels in blood cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C-D showing elevated iGABA levels in Gat over-expressing condition.

claim: Progenitor-specific expression of αKDHRNAi does not affect circulating lamellocyte formation at 48HPI.
source: Quantifications of total circulating lamellocyte per sample in dome-MESO-Gal4, UAS-GFP/+ (control, n = 35), dome-MESO-Gal4, UAS-GFP; UAS-αKDHRNAi (n = 25, ns)
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 5B with statistical analysis showing no significant difference (ns).

claim: Sima protein expression is detected at basal levels in all cells of the larval lymph gland and cells of the PSC.
source: Within the Drosophila larval hematopoietic tissue, Sima protein, orthologous to mammalian HIF1α (Lavista-Llanos et al., 2002) is detected at basal levels in all cells of the larval lymph gland and cells of the PSC (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B)
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-B showing Sima protein expression patterns.

claim: Within 6 hours of wasp-infection, a twofold upregulation in expression of Sima protein in lymph gland blood cells is observed.
source: Within a few hours of wasp-infection (6HPI), a twofold upregulation in expression of Sima protein in lymph gland blood cells was noticed (Figure 3B and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3B and quantification in Figure 3E showing twofold increase in Sima protein expression at 6HPI.

claim: Sima protein expression is detected in lamellocytes at 12HPI and 24HPI.
source: Later, when formation of lamellocyte was detected (12HPI and 24 HPI), Sima protein expression was seen in them as well (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E–H').
evidence: The claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E-H' showing Sima protein expression in lamellocytes.

claim: The increase in Sima protein levels in response to infection does not correlate with a similar increase in sima mRNA levels at 6HPI.
source: The increase in Sima protein levels in response to infection did not corroborate with a similar increase in sima mRNA levels at 6HPI, when only a mild increase in sima mRNA levels was noticed (Figure 3—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1I showing only mild increase in sima mRNA levels at 6HPI.

claim: Expressing simaRNAi in progenitor cells causes reduction in lamellocyte numbers in circulation at 48HPI.
source: Quantifications of circulating lamellocyte counts in dome-MESO-Gal4, UAS-GFP/+ (control, n = 20), dome-MESO-Gal4, UAS-GFP; UAS-simaRNAi (n = 29, ***p<0.0001)
evidence: The claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 3U with statistical analysis (p<0.0001).

claim: Ldh mRNA expression shows a 30-fold increase in lymph glands post-wasp-infection at 6HPI.
source: We observed a 30-fold increase in Ldh mRNA expression in lymph glands post-wasp-infection (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A showing 30-fold increase in Ldh mRNA expression.

claim: Neuronally released GABA derived upon olfactory stimulation is utilized by blood-progenitor cells as a metabolite.
source: We show that neuronally released GABA derived upon olfactory stimulation is utilized by blood-progenitor cells as a metabolite and through its catabolism, these cells stabilize Sima/HIFα protein.
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple experimental data showing GABA uptake via Gat, its catabolism via Ssadh, and the resulting stabilization of Sima protein in blood-progenitor cells.

claim: GABA catabolism in blood-progenitor cells stabilizes Sima/HIFα protein.
source: We show that neuronally released GABA derived upon olfactory stimulation is utilized by blood-progenitor cells as a metabolite and through its catabolism, these cells stabilize Sima/HIFα protein.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing that blocking GABA catabolism (via GatRNAi or SsadhRNAi) reduces Sima protein levels, and succinate supplementation restores Sima levels.

claim: Sima capacitates blood-progenitor cells with the ability to initiate lamellocyte differentiation.
source: Sima capacitates blood-progenitor cells with the ability to initiate lamellocyte differentiation.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing that loss of Sima function (simaRNAi) severely impairs lamellocyte formation, while conditions that increase Sima levels (Gat overexpression, succinate supplementation) enhance lamellocyte formation.

claim: Animals dwelling in wasp-infested environments elevate their systemic GABA levels leading to upregulation of blood-progenitor cell Sima expression.
source: By co-opting the olfactory route, the preconditioned animals elevate their systemic GABA levels leading to the upregulation of blood-progenitor cell Sima expression.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing that animals reared on wasp-odor food (WOF) have elevated hemolymph GABA levels, increased lymph gland iGABA, and increased Sima protein expression.

claim: Elevated Sima expression in preconditioned animals elevates their immune-potential and primes them to respond rapidly when infected with parasitic wasps.
source: This elevates their immune-potential and primes them to respond rapidly when infected with parasitic wasps.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing that WOF animals have increased lamellocyte numbers, improved encapsulation response, and increased melanization response compared to control animals.

claim: Lamellocytes appear upon infections with the parasitic wasp, Leptopilina boulardi.
source: Of these, lamellocytes which are undetectable in healthy animals, appear upon infections with the parasitic wasp, Leptopilina boulardi (L. boulardi) which triggers their development (Crozatier et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Crozatier et al., 2004) and is consistent with the experimental observations in the manuscript.

claim: Within a few hours of wasp-egg deposition, the Drosophila larval hematopoietic system activates a series of cellular innate immune responses leading to massive differentiation of blood cells into lamellocytes.
source: Within a few hours of wasp-egg deposition, the Drosophila larval hematopoietic system activates a series of cellular innate immune responses leading to massive differentiation of blood cells into lamellocytes.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental observations showing lamellocyte formation at 24HPI in lymph gland and 48HPI in circulation, and is consistent with cited literature.

claim: Lamellocyte differentiation includes trans-differentiation of circulating and sessile plasmatocytes and differentiation of multipotent blood-progenitor cells of the lymph gland.
source: This includes trans-differentiation of circulating and sessile plasmatocytes and differentiation of multipotent blood-progenitor cells of the larval hematopoietic organ termed the 'lymph gland' (Anderl et al., 2016; Honti et al., 2010; Márkus et al., 2009; Stofanko et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work (Anderl et al., 2016; Honti et al., 2010; Márkus et al., 2009; Stofanko et al., 2010).

claim: As lymph gland progenitor cells differentiate, the gland ultimately disintegrates to release its blood cells into circulation.
source: As lymph gland progenitor cells differentiate, the gland ultimately disintegrates to release its blood cells into circulation (Lanot et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Lanot et al., 2001).

claim: Lamellocyte numbers reach a maximum at 48 hr after wasp-egg laying.
source: Together, these events contribute toward robust lamellocyte numbers which reach a maximum at 48 hr after wasp-egg laying (Lanot et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Lanot et al., 2001) and is consistent with the experimental design in the manuscript analyzing circulating lamellocytes at 48HPI.

claim: Lamellocytes encapsulate the deposited wasp-eggs and melanize them, facilitating their effective clearance.
source: Characterized by their large flattened appearance, lamellocytes encapsulate the deposited wasp-eggs and melanize them, facilitating their effective clearance (Rizki and Rizki, 1992).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Rizki and Rizki, 1992) and is consistent with the encapsulation and melanization assays performed in the manuscript.

claim: Olfactory signaling has been implicated in the maintenance of multipotent blood-progenitor cells of the lymph gland.
source: Of these, olfactory signaling has been implicated in their maintenance (Shim et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Shim et al., 2013).

claim: The Drosophila larval olfactory system contains 25 specific odorant receptors (OR) in 21 olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs).
source: The Drosophila larval olfactory system contains 25 specific odorant receptors (OR) in 21 olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs).
evidence: The claim represents established knowledge about the Drosophila larval olfactory system.

claim: Orco (Or83b), an atypical OR protein, expressed in every ORN is necessary to respond to all odors.
source: Orco (Or83b), an atypical OR protein, expressed in every ORN is necessary to respond to all odors.
evidence: The claim represents established knowledge about Orco function and is supported by the experimental use of orco mutants in the manuscript.

claim: During Drosophila larval development, olfaction stimulates the release of GABA from neurosecretory cells of the brain, which systemically activates GABABR signaling in the progenitor cells to support their maintenance.
source: It has been previously shown that during Drosophila larval development, olfaction stimulates the release of GABA from neurosecretory cells of the brain, which systemically activates GABABR signaling in the progenitor cells to support their maintenance (Shim et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Shim et al., 2013).

claim: In animals with olfactory dysfunction, the systemic cross-talk between olfaction and hematopoiesis is perturbed and drives precocious differentiation of blood-progenitor cells.
source: In animals with olfactory dysfunction, this systemic cross-talk is perturbed and drives precocious differentiation of blood-progenitor cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Shim et al., 2013) and is consistent with the experimental observations in the manuscript.

claim: Sima is a well-characterized transcription factor known for its role in inducing hypoxia response.
source: Sima is a well-characterized transcription factor known for its role in inducing hypoxia response (Romero et al., 2007; Semenza and Wang, 1992)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous work (Romero et al., 2007; Semenza and Wang, 1992).

claim: Sima in immune progenitor cells is necessary to drive lamellocyte differentiation.
source: Sima is a well-characterized transcription factor known for its role in inducing hypoxia response (Romero et al., 2007; Semenza and Wang, 1992), which in immune progenitor cells is necessary to drive lamellocyte differentiation.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing that loss of Sima function (simaRNAi) severely impairs lamellocyte formation.
